content.content:
1	# D.110c-0c1f5b0p removed-author identity-history source audit
2	
3	## Anchor and scope
4	
5	- Audited signed/pushed commit and upstream:
6	  `e6a67013b1f64b7ea2155f59a3d578f52ed84ed6`.
7	- Audited tree: `488075c6ee680c48e22b639a44957cabd038cb00`.
8	- Branch: `codex/phase3a1b-p6-golden-path`.
9	- This is a plan/design checkpoint only. It changes no production source,
10	  dependency, wire bytes, API, threshold, workload, test, campaign, or consumed
11	  invocation.
12	- The rejected first f5b0 review and its immutable evidence remain under
13	  `.logs/d110c-0c1f5b0-plan-review-fc4b8fc7/`. This audit addresses the one
14	  blocking removed-key reset problem isolated by the signed amendment at this
15	  anchor; it does not reopen accepted D.110c evidence.
16	
17	## Current production owners
18	
19	1. `packages/protocol-v3/src/latched-acl.ts:120-166` accepts only the current
20	   canonical ACL and caps it at 64 members. `freezeMembers()` at lines 351-368
21	   removes a key after its last role/finality key is revoked. Grant/revoke
22	   staging at lines 376-446 carries no incarnation, prior-appearance bit, or
23	   sequence boundary. A later grant of the same 32-byte public key is therefore
24	   indistinguishable from a globally fresh key at this owner.
25	2. The creator settlement checkpoint proposed by f5b0 can keep exact
26	   `admittedThrough` and `settledThrough` values for current members, but an
27	   omitted removed member loses those authenticated facts. Caller-local
28	   issuance lineage cannot repair this because it is not creator authority and
29	   may be absent on a cold creator restart.
30	3. `packages/compaction/src/history-commitment.ts` implements an RFC 9162
31	   ordinal append-only history commitment. Its leaves bind epoch, object,
32	   ordinal and vertex hash. It can prove inclusion/consistency of a known
33	   historical leaf, but it has no public-key index and cannot prove that a key
34	   never appeared or find that key's last boundary without an additional
35	   authenticated index.
36	4. `archiveIndexRoot` is carried through anchors, cuts and snapshots, but the
37	   audited production paths expose no implemented author-keyed index or proof
38	   owner behind that digest. Treating the field name as an existing capability
39	   would be a fixture shortcut.
40	5. `AheDurableStore` in `packages/storage/src/types.ts:110-150` owns generation
41	   blobs referenced by an explicit flat closure. The closure verifier at
42	   `packages/storage/src/internal/closure-verifier.ts:55-122` checks only each
43	   listed reference's promotion, byte length and digest. Browser reclamation
44	   derives live blobs from those explicit generation/promotion rows; it does
45	   not traverse child references inside an indirect authenticated tree.
46	   Storing a Merkle tree behind one AHE root blob would therefore either leak
47	   nodes or permit reclamation of reachable nodes. A separate store contract
48	   and reachability owner is required.
49	6. The fixed creator trust profile is currently hard-coded as
50	   `creator-trusted-v1` in protocol trust, creator close, Node live/close and
51	   room successor authority. The exact profile bytes are hashed into the
52	   genesis anchor and carried unchanged by successors. A runtime-only
53	   settlement switch is therefore not genesis-authenticated and would allow an
54	   old binary to close the same invite using the legacy rules.
55	7. The room invite already transports exact canonical profile bytes and the
56	   pinned, creator-signed genesis anchor. A sibling genesis profile can be
57	   authenticated without changing the invite envelope or public-key authority,
58	   but accepting that profile is still an explicit protocol/public
59	   compatibility change and must be reviewed before implementation.
60	
61	## Capability conclusion
62	
63	No current component can authenticate both prior nonappearance and the last
64	boundary for an arbitrary removed public key in sublinear room-age work. The
65	missing seam is not composition over a dormant implementation. With ordinary
66	hash primitives, the information must live in an explicitly counted
67	authenticated dictionary; a constant-size checkpoint can commit to that
68	dictionary, but the dictionary backing necessarily grows with the number of
69	currently retired distinct keys. A construction that also makes the backing
70	constant-size needs a stronger accumulator/recursive-proof assumption.
71	
72	The selected existing-primitive construction is a creator-authenticated,
73	content-addressed Merkle AVL dictionary of **currently retired** keys. Its root
74	and entry count live in the creator settlement checkpoint. The current active
75	checkpoint remains bounded by the 64-member ACL; ordinary cold reopen does not
76	load or replay dictionary nodes. The creator needs verified O(log R) paths only
77	when an ACL transition removes or re-adds a key, where `R` is the number of
78	currently retired distinct keys. Missing backing state is an availability
79	failure for that membership-changing close, never permission to treat a key as
80	fresh.
81	
82	Every child reference also authenticates its height, subtree size and min/max

  `.logs/d110c-0c1f5b0-plan-review-fc4b8fc7/`. This audit addresses the one
  blocking removed-key reset problem isolated by the signed amendment at this
  anchor; it does not reopen accepted D.110c evidence.

## Current production owners

1. `packages/protocol-v3/src/latched-acl.ts:120-166` accepts only the current
   canonical ACL and caps it at 64 members. `freezeMembers()` at lines 351-368
   removes a key after its last role/finality key is revoked. Grant/revoke
   staging at lines 376-446 carries no incarnation, prior-appearance bit, or
   sequence boundary. A later grant of the same 32-byte public key is therefore
   indistinguishable from a globally fresh key at this owner.
2. The creator settlement checkpoint proposed by f5b0 can keep exact
   `admittedThrough` and `settledThrough` values for current members, but an
   omitted removed member loses those authenticated facts. Caller-local
   issuance lineage cannot repair this because it is not creator authority and
   may be absent on a cold creator restart.
3. `packages/compaction/src/history-commitment.ts` implements an RFC 9162
   ordinal append-only history commitment. Its leaves bind epoch, object,
   ordinal and vertex hash. It can prove inclusion/consistency of a known
   historical leaf, but it has no public-key index and cannot prove that a key
   never appeared or find that key's last boundary without an additional
   authenticated index.
4. `archiveIndexRoot` is carried through anchors, cuts and snapshots, but the
   audited production paths expose no implemented author-keyed index or proof
   owner behind that digest. Treating the field name as an existing capability
   would be a fixture shortcut.
5. `AheDurableStore` in `packages/storage/src/types.ts:110-150` owns generation
   blobs referenced by an explicit flat closure. The closure verifier at
   `packages/storage/src/internal/closure-verifier.ts:55-122` checks only each
   listed reference's promotion, byte length and digest. Browser reclamation
   derives live blobs from those explicit generation/promotion rows; it does
   not traverse child references inside an indirect authenticated tree.
   Storing a Merkle tree behind one AHE root blob would therefore either leak
   nodes or permit reclamation of reachable nodes. A separate store contract
   and reachability owner is required.
6. The fixed creator trust profile is currently hard-coded as
   `creator-trusted-v1` in protocol trust, creator close, Node live/close and
   room successor authority. The exact profile bytes are hashed into the
   genesis anchor and carried unchanged by successors. A runtime-only
   settlement switch is therefore not genesis-authenticated and would allow an
   old binary to close the same invite using the legacy rules.
7. The room invite already transports exact canonical profile bytes and the
   pinned, creator-signed genesis anchor. A sibling genesis profile can be
   authenticated without changing the invite envelope or public-key authority,
   but accepting that profile is still an explicit protocol/public
   compatibility change and must be reviewed before implementation.

No current component can authenticate both prior nonappearance and the last
boundary for an arbitrary removed public key in sublinear room-age work. The
missing seam is not composition over a dormant implementation. With ordinary
hash primitives, the information must live in an explicitly counted
authenticated dictionary; a constant-size checkpoint can commit to that
dictionary, but the dictionary backing necessarily grows with the number of
currently retired distinct keys. A construction that also makes the backing
constant-size needs a stronger accumulator/recursive-proof assumption.

The selected existing-primitive construction is a creator-authenticated,
content-addressed Merkle AVL dictionary of **currently retired** keys. Its root
and entry count live in the creator settlement checkpoint. The current active
checkpoint remains bounded by the 64-member ACL; ordinary cold reopen does not
load or replay dictionary nodes. The creator needs verified O(log R) paths only
when an ACL transition removes or re-adds a key, where `R` is the number of
currently retired distinct keys. Missing backing state is an availability
failure for that membership-changing close, never permission to treat a key as

ordering and metadata without opening an entire sibling subtree. Safe-integer
entry count bounds an AVL path to 76 nodes. A maximum 64-insert/64-delete
transition, allowing a second in-order-successor path for every two-child

shared node bytes are carried once.

counted archive-tier control index of O(R) entries, not active bootstrap state

current and two rollback roots are reclaimable. The live dictionary cannot be
pruned below the information needed to reject a reset. If the governing review
requires O(1) durable bytes even under unbounded distinct-key churn, this hash-

proof prerequisite rather than disguising the growth.

support mandatory from epoch zero. Existing `creator-trusted-v1` rooms and
bytes remain unchanged and cannot late-opt-in in this slice. Old binaries fail
closed on the unsupported profile. This eliminates the unsafe attempt to infer
settled or removed-author state from a legacy room whose complete historical

authority. It does add an explicit profile identifier and widens internal/public
profile unions that currently contain only `creator-trusted-v1`; that change is
part of this high-risk prerequisite and remains unauthorized until the combined

two-child registry node is 792 bytes (232 bytes below its proposed 1,024-byte

1	# D.110c-0c1f5b0p bounded removed-author identity-history design
2	
3	## Decision
4	
5	Select a deterministic creator-authenticated Merkle AVL dictionary of currently
6	retired public keys and bind its root/count into every settlement checkpoint.
7	Select a new genesis-bound `creator-trusted-settlement-v1` profile so settlement
8	and retired-key continuity start at epoch zero. Do not migrate an existing
9	`creator-trusted-v1` room in this slice.
10	
11	This remains a high-risk audited recommendation, not production authorization.
12	It adds no cryptographic dependency or setup and preserves the fixed creator
13	signer, Ed25519/SHA-256, cut/QC, ACL, anchor, snapshot, history and availability
14	authority. It does add a profile identifier, settlement/checkpoint schemas and
15	a storage-neutral retired-author registry contract. Those changes require the
16	combined f5b0p/f5b0 confirmation before tests-only RED.
17	
18	## Authenticated dictionary
19	
20	### Canonical node and root
21	
22	The empty root is
23	`hex(hashDomain("ts-drp/retired-author-registry-empty/v1", encodeCanonical(null)))`.
24	Every nonempty node is the exact canonical record:
25	
26	```ts
27	{
28		author: string,
29		admittedThrough: number | null,
30		height: number,
31		kind: "drp-retired-author-registry-node",
32		left: {
33			byteLength: number,
34			digest: string,
35			height: number,
36			maxAuthor: string,
37			minAuthor: string,
38			subtreeSize: number,
39		} | null,
40		right: {
41			byteLength: number,
42			digest: string,
43			height: number,
44			maxAuthor: string,
45			minAuthor: string,
46			subtreeSize: number,
47		} | null,
48		settledThrough: number | null,
49		subtreeSize: number,
50		version: 1,
51	}
52	```
53	
54	`author` is exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Non-null boundaries
55	are safe nonnegative integers; `settledThrough` may not exceed
56	`admittedThrough`, and `admittedThrough === null` requires
57	`settledThrough === null`. Height and subtree size are safe positive integers
58	recomputed from children. A child reference has the six exact keys shown,
59	positive safe byte length/height/subtree size, lowercase 64-hex digest and
60	canonical min/max 64-hex keys. Parent height, size and extrema must recompute
61	exactly from those child facts, with `left.maxAuthor < author <
62	right.minAuthor`. Node digest is
63	`hex(hashDomain("ts-drp/retired-author-registry-node/v1", exactCanonicalNodeBytes))`.
64	Nodes have a 1,024-byte ceiling.
65	
66	The exact maximum-shaped two-child node encoded with the workspace canonical
67	implementation is 792 bytes, leaving 232 bytes under that ceiling.
68	
69	The tree is a strict binary-search tree under UTF-16 code-unit order and an AVL
70	tree with balance factor -1, 0 or 1. Heights, subtree sizes, extrema, child byte
71	lengths, digests, key ordering and canonical bytes are recomputed along every
72	opened path; authenticated unopened-child metadata supplies the sibling facts
73	needed for parent recomputation. Empty and nonempty roots are unambiguous.
74	
75	### Proofs and deterministic updates
76	
77	A lookup proof contains the exact root-to-terminal node bytes. The verifier
78	rehashes every node, follows only the branch selected by the queried key,
79	checks all AVL/order/metadata constraints exposed by the path, and ends either
80	at the unique matching key or at a null child. A truncated path, extra node,
81	wrong branch, foreign root, noncanonical node, digest/length mismatch,
82	duplicate key or malformed boundary fails closed. Membership returns the exact
83	prior boundaries; nonmembership returns no boundaries.
84	
85	A batch witness is a canonical digest-keyed set of node bytes plus an ordered
86	mutation-to-path schedule. Each mutation path is verified against the root
87	produced by the preceding mutation, not only the original root. Deleting a node
88	with two children additionally opens the deterministic in-order-successor path;
89	missing or surplus scheduled nodes fail. Shared nodes appear once in the node
90	set and may be referenced repeatedly by digest.
91	
92	The detached canonical witness has this exact tests-and-store boundary (it is
93	not a vertex, checkpoint field or public network record):
94	
95	```ts
96	type RetiredAuthorBatchWitness = {
97		kind: "drp-retired-author-registry-batch-witness";
98		mutationsDigest: string;
99		nodes: readonly [digest: string, exactCanonicalNodeBytes: Uint8Array][];
100		priorRoot: string;
101		priorRootSize: number;
102		steps: readonly {
103			author: string;
104			lookupPath: readonly string[];
105			successorPath: readonly string[];
106		}[];
107		version: 1;
108	};
109	```
110	
111	`nodes` are strictly digest-sorted and unique. Every path item names one entry
112	in that map or one node computed by an earlier step. `steps` correspond one-to-
113	one with mutations in the same order. `successorPath` is empty except for a
114	two-child delete. The witness digest is
115	`hashDomain("ts-drp/retired-author-registry-batch-witness/v1", bytes)` and the
116	mutation digest uses
117	`ts-drp/retired-author-registry-mutations/v1`. Witness canonical bytes are
118	capped at 20,971,520; node count, path count and node-byte limits are checked
119	before allocation.
120	
121	A transition is an exact code-unit-sorted, unique batch of at most 128
122	mutations, the maximum possible current-ACL-to-successor-ACL difference with
123	both ACLs capped at 64:
124	
125	```ts
126	type RetiredAuthorMutation =
127		| {
128				author: string;
129				expected: "absent";
130				kind: "assert-absent";
131		  }
132		| {
133				author: string;
134				expected: "absent";
135				kind: "insert";
136				admittedThrough: number | null;
137				settledThrough: number | null;
138		  }
139		| { author: string; expected: { admittedThrough: number | null; settledThrough: number | null }; kind: "delete" };
140	```
141	
142	No assertion/insertion accepts an occupied key, no update overwrites an
143	occupied key and no delete accepts absent or different boundaries. An
144	`assert-absent` step leaves the root/count unchanged. The pure transition
145	verifier applies mutations in order using canonical AVL insertion/deletion and
146	deterministic single/double rotations.
147	Given the prior root/count, exact verified path nodes and mutations, every
148	conforming implementation must derive the same successor root/count and the
149	same newly reachable node bytes. The successor count must equal prior count
150	plus inserts minus deletes and remain a safe integer.
151	
152	Proof length is O(log R), where `R` is the prior retired-key count; update work
153	and newly written nodes are O(M log R) for `M <= 128`. With safe-integer
154	`subtreeSize`, an AVL path has at most 76 nodes. One maximum transition has at
155	most 64 insertions and 64 deletions; a two-child deletion may need two paths.
156	It therefore schedules at most 14,592 node visits and at most 14,942,208
157	canonical node bytes under the 1,024-byte node ceiling; shared node bytes are
158	transmitted once.
159	The record does not set a room-age-dependent proof-byte threshold. Existing
160	epoch byte/capacity limits remain unchanged because proofs are creator/store
161	inputs, not vertices, checkpoint fields or application operations.
162	Implementations stream/iterate paths and may not materialize the complete
163	dictionary. The retained browser gate records measured maximum proof bytes,
164	update bytes and peak owned memory for the reviewed 100-transition workload;
165	it does not turn an observation into a new protocol ceiling.
166	
167	## ACL transition law
168	
169	For each authenticated current/successor ACL pair, derive sets by public key:
170	
171	- retained member: copy its exact active frontier; dictionary is unchanged;
172	- removed member: insert its exact current
173	  `{admittedThrough,settledThrough}` into an absent dictionary key;
174	- added member with dictionary membership: delete the exact entry and restore
175	  those boundaries into the active successor frontier; its next authored
176	  sequence must be strictly above `admittedThrough`;
177	- added member with verified dictionary nonmembership: require an
178	  `assert-absent` step and begin with both boundaries null, so its first
179	  sequence is zero; and
180	- absent in both: no active or dictionary change.
181	
182	No key may be active and retired in the same successor state. A key removed and
183	re-added by multiple operations within one staged ACL is classified only from
184	the authenticated current and final successor snapshots; if present in both it
185	is retained and cannot reset. Permission changes that leave any role/finality
186	key retain the active frontier. Permissionless writer behavior does not bypass
187	identity continuity.
188	
189	The creator settlement owner verifies the prior checkpoint and dictionary root,
190	derives this exact diff, asks the registry store for proofs, independently runs
191	the pure verifier, and durably installs the successor registry state before it
192	signs the successor settlement checkpoint. A missing/corrupt/stale path,
193	unknown transaction outcome or durability failure aborts the membership-
194	changing close before signature. An ACL-unchanged close copies the exact root
195	and count without opening the store.
196	
197	The fixed creator signature attests the resulting current root to ordinary
198	openers under the already selected D.110c-0b trust model. Non-creator openers do
199	not need dictionary paths to authenticate the current ACL/frontiers. This does
200	not make a self-signed root trusted: the root/count are inside the exact creator
201	checkpoint, which is bound to the pinned genesis carrier, object, profile,
202	anchors, ACLs, close cut/QC, snapshot and history.
203	
204	## Store contract and custody
205	
206	Add a storage-neutral `RetiredAuthorRegistryStore` capability with opaque,
207	closed inputs/results for:
208	
209	1. `prove({objectId,root,rootSize,authors})`: return detached canonical path
210	   nodes for sorted unique authors without mutating state;
211	2. `transactTransition({objectId,expectedRoot,expectedRootSize,retainRoots,mutations})`:
212	   strict-durability CAS from one registered current root, validate/rederive the
213	   pure transition, write all new content-addressed nodes, register the new
214	   root/count, and return an immutable receipt containing prior/successor
215	   root/count, mutation digest and exact batch-witness digest; and
216	3. `reclaim({objectId,currentRoot,rollbackRoots})`: mark from exactly the
217	   authenticated current root plus at most two authenticated rollback roots and
218	   delete other nodes/root registrations atomically.
219	
220	The in-memory reference implementation and the browser IndexedDB implementation
221	are conformant. The browser owner uses a dedicated derived database/schema with
222	strict transactions, content-addressed `nodes` and object-scoped `roots`; it is
223	not an untracked side table inside AHE. Opening validates schema/incarnation.
224	Every read rechecks canonical bytes/digest/length. Root registrations are
225	exactly `candidate | current | rollback`; one serialized object may have at
226	most one candidate, one current and two rollback roots. Conflicting bytes for
227	one digest, root/count disagreement, an unclassified registered root, partial
228	writes, CAS mismatch or ambiguous commit poison/fail closed until authenticated
229	recovery determines whether the exact transition committed.
230	
231	Write-before-sign ordering is mandatory:
232	
233	1. authenticate current settlement checkpoint and both ACLs;
234	2. derive mutations and verify prior paths;
235	3. strictly commit/register successor root;
236	4. stage/sign/publish close and successor checkpoint;
237	5. adopt and install the authenticated successor;
238	6. retain current plus two rollback registry roots while matching rollback
239	   generations remain required; and
240	7. reclaim unreachable old nodes only after adoption, room-head/freshness,
241	   snapshot, rollback and availability gates pass.
242	
243	A crash after step 3 but before signature leaves the sole inert candidate root;
244	retry with the same expected root/mutations/witness digest is idempotent and
245	may reuse it. A different transition is refused until the candidate is
246	authenticated and either matched to a checkpoint or discarded from the still-
247	current prior root. A crash
248	after signature but before adoption retains both roots. A missing current-root
249	node after restart is corruption/availability failure, never nonmembership.
250	Unknown write outcome is resolved by authenticating the registered exact
251	successor root/count/mutation/witness digest; blind retry is forbidden.
252	
253	Reachable nodes under the current root grow O(R). They are explicitly counted
254	as an archive-tier control index. They are not loaded for ordinary issue,
255	publish, projection, current-checkpoint verification, restart or cold reopen.
256	They are required only for creator-authorized ACL membership change and may be
257	fetched from untrusted content storage because every byte is verified against
258	the creator-authenticated root. If unavailable, that ACL-changing close stalls;
259	ordinary room use under the current ACL continues. Phase 7 may mirror/page the
260	same content-addressed nodes but may not redefine their authentication.
261	
262	## Genesis-bound profile and compatibility
263	
264	Add profile ID `creator-trusted-settlement-v1`. Its canonical profile keys,
265	crypto suite, one signer, quorum and signer-set binding are identical to
266	`creator-trusted-v1`; only the profile ID differs. The genesis anchor's existing
267	`profileDigest` authenticates the choice. Internal trust values and the room's
268	successor authority widen to the exact union
269	`"creator-trusted-v1" | "creator-trusted-settlement-v1"`; the UI trust text
270	remains creator-trusted/not-BFT because authority did not change.
271	
272	Under `creator-trusted-settlement-v1`:
273	
274	- the implicit authenticated genesis sentinel supplies current ACL members
275	  with null boundaries and the empty retired root/size zero; there is no
276	  separate genesis settlement record;
277	- the first close emits the first settlement checkpoint directly;
278	- every later close requires exactly one settlement checkpoint;
279	- the v1 admitted-frontier aggregate and legacy creator retirement record are
280	  never emitted or accepted; and
281	- `$drp.author-settlement.v1` is mandatory from the first epoch in which a
282	  source disposition is needed.
283	
284	Under `creator-trusted-v1`, all existing bytes and behavior remain unchanged;
285	settlement checkpoint/control kinds are rejected. There is no runtime option,
286	negotiation, downgrade or late opt-in. Existing v1 rooms cannot migrate here
287	because their removed-author history is not authenticated by a keyed index.
288	A future migration would need a separately reviewed full-history/archive proof
289	that reconstructs the registry without omission; Phase 7 may own that work.
290	
291	The invite envelope, signer set, public key, anchor schema, CutValue, QC and
292	vertex envelope are unchanged. The new profile identifier is nevertheless a
293	public compatibility addition: old binaries reject it, and room creators must
294	choose it when producing the genesis profile bytes. This checkpoint does not
295	silently make it the default for existing callers.
296	
297	This is a prospective profile-inventory amendment. Earlier Phase-3 acceptance
298	that supported exactly the then-existing three profiles remains immutable
299	historical evidence; after this slice GREEN, the supported inventory adds this
300	fourth creator-only sibling for newly created settlement rooms. It does not
301	reinterpret a prior profile, reopen its tests or claim old binaries support the
302	new ID.
303	
304	## Settlement checkpoint amendment
305	
306	Replace the previously proposed checkpoint's migration fields with this exact
307	shape (signature appended after signing):
308	
309	```ts
310	{
311		closedAnchorDigest,
312		closedEpoch,
313		commitQcRef: { byteLength, digest },
314		currentAclDigest,
315		cutValueDigest,
316		frontiers: readonly [author, admittedThrough, settledThrough][],
317		genesisAnchorDigest,
318		historyRoot,
319		historySize,
320		kind: "drp-creator-author-settlement-state",
321		objectId,
322		priorCheckpointDigest,
323		priorCheckpointKind: "genesis" | "settled-v1",
324		protocolMajor: 3,
325		retiredAuthorRegistryRoot,
326		retiredAuthorRegistrySize,
327		snapshotManifestDigest,
328		successorAclDigest,
329		successorAnchorDigest,
330		successorEpoch,
331		version: 1,
332	}
333	```
334	
335	`retiredAuthorRegistryRoot` is the exact empty or node digest;
336	`retiredAuthorRegistrySize` is a safe nonnegative integer. The current active
337	frontier has exactly the successor ACL's sorted unique members, at most 64.
338	The profile must be `creator-trusted-settlement-v1`. Genesis is the sole
339	sentinel predecessor; every non-genesis predecessor is one adjacent settlement
340	checkpoint under the same profile/object/genesis. There is no
341	`admitted-v1` predecessor, v1 migration branch or legacy-retirement bridge.
342	The maximum-shaped signed checkpoint with 64 full frontier entries, a 256-code-
343	unit object ID, maximum safe integers, full digests and a 64-byte creator
344	signature encodes to 7,064 bytes with the workspace canonical implementation,
345	leaving 1,128 bytes under the unchanged 8,192-byte ceiling. Codec RED must pin
346	that exact measurement and adjacent over-limit/count rejection; the ceiling is
347	not raised.
348	
349	## Failure and adversarial matrix
350	
351	| Case                                                         | Required result                                                                             |
352	| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
353	| globally fresh key                                           | verified nonmembership; null boundaries; first sequence zero                                |
354	| removed key re-added                                         | membership restores exact boundaries; next sequence strictly greater than admitted boundary |
355	| key retained across ACL roles                                | active boundary copied; no dictionary mutation                                              |
356	| remove then re-add within one staged ACL                     | retained by current/final membership; no reset                                              |
357	| active key also found in retired root                        | checkpoint/transition invalid                                                               |
358	| insertion finds occupied key                                 | fail closed; no checkpoint signature                                                        |
359	| deletion finds absent/different boundaries                   | fail closed; no checkpoint signature                                                        |
360	| stale, substituted, truncated, reordered or foreign proof    | fail closed before store mutation/signature                                                 |
361	| noncanonical node or wrong digest/length/height/size/balance | fail closed and classify store corruption                                                   |
362	| store unavailable                                            | membership-changing close unavailable; no fallback-to-fresh                                 |
363	| crash before registry commit                                 | old root remains current; retry from durable truth                                          |
364	| crash after registry commit before checkpoint signature      | inert candidate root; idempotent exact retry or later GC                                    |
365	| crash after signature before adoption                        | both roots retained; old checkpoint authoritative                                           |
366	| adoption succeeds before reclamation                         | new root authoritative; rollback roots still retained                                       |
367	| premature/misbound reclamation                               | CAS/reachability refusal; no live-node deletion                                             |
368	| old profile receives new carrier                             | unsupported/mixed-profile rejection                                                         |
369	| new profile omits settlement/registry carrier                | fail closed                                                                                 |
370	| legacy room attempts late opt-in                             | explicit unsupported migration failure                                                      |
371	| untrusted current checkpoint nominates its own key/root      | rejected by pinned-genesis creator-trust opener                                             |
372	| valid but stale checkpoint/root                              | rejected by the existing external room-head freshness floor                                 |
373	
374	## Bounds and golden-path accounting
375	
376	- Active settlement checkpoint: O(64) frontier entries plus one root/count;
377	  independent of epoch, rebase count and retired-author count.
378	- Ordinary hot issue/publish and cold reopen: no dictionary traversal; fixed
379	  checkpoint plus existing current/two-rollback closure law.
380	- Membership-changing close: O(M log R) verified reads/writes for `M <= 128`;
381	  no O(epoch) or O(history) replay.
382	- Reachable registry backing: O(R) entries/bytes for currently retired distinct
383	  keys, plus copy-on-write nodes reachable from at most two rollback roots and
384	  at most one serialized candidate root.
385	  This is separately reported in the durable census by entry count, node count
386	  and bytes. It is never counted as application archive or hidden bootstrap.
387	- Re-adding a retired key deletes its live registry entry; removing it later
388	  inserts the newer boundary. Repeated churn of a fixed author set therefore
389	  keeps current-root logical entries bounded by that set, while obsolete path
390	  nodes are reclaimable after rollback gates.
391	- The ≥100 same-room transition test includes remove/re-add, fresh additions,
392	  restarts before/after registry commit and adoption, selected prune boundaries,
393	  exact root/count recomputation, current/rollback reachability census and a
394	  fresh-process post-GC memory gate. It does not claim O(1) archival registry
395	  bytes under unbounded distinct-key churn.
396	
397	## TDD slices and gates
398	
399	After the combined design confirmation is empty at P0/P1:
400	
401	1. **f5b0p-a protocol dictionary/profile RED→GREEN.** Tests-only RED exercises
402	   empty/member/nonmember proofs, deterministic AVL rotations, batch updates,
403	   stale/substituted proofs, root/count/metadata corruption, maximum 128-key
404	   transition, profile acceptance/rejection and the measured 64-frontier
405	   checkpoint ceiling. GREEN is confined to pure codecs/verifiers/profile
406	   unions/exports and adds no storage or room behavior.
407	2. **f5b0p-b store RED→GREEN.** Tests-only RED freezes in-memory and browser
408	   conformance, strict write-before-sign receipt semantics, idempotence,
409	   ambiguous commit recovery, corruption poison, current/two-rollback
410	   reachability GC and unavailable-node refusal. GREEN adds the neutral store,
411	   memory implementation, dedicated IndexedDB implementation/schema and
412	   internal room construction plumbing; it does not integrate creator close.
413	3. **f5b0a-d and f5b.** Resume the already frozen settlement carrier, Node,
414	   room and pruning slices, amended so new-profile genesis has no v1 migration
415	   or legacy retirement. Creator integration uses the genuine ACL diff and
416	   registry store before signing. Each retains its causal RED and focused,
417	   static, retained and isolated GREEN gates.
418	
419	The combined functional RED must fail through the real product path: create a
420	`creator-trusted-settlement-v1` room, remove an author after admitted/settled
421	activity, close/adopt/restart, re-add the same key and attempt sequence zero.
422	It must also show a truly fresh key starts at zero. Fixture-injected registry
423	roots or tests-only appearance facts cannot satisfy causality.
424	
425	GREEN/retained acceptance includes exact same-key continuation, fresh-key zero,
426	mixed ACL role retention, 64-member/128-mutation bounds, store-death crash
427	matrix, two rollback roots, unavailable registry refusal, ordinary reopen with
428	the registry store absent, no v1 behavior change, old-binary profile rejection,
429	current checkpoint byte ceiling, ≥100 real same-room epochs, bounded active
430	checkpoint/owner census, explicit O(R) registry census, and Phase-7 cold join
431	using current authenticated checkpoint plus archived application history.
432	
433	No production edit, RED, long campaign or multi-epoch run is authorized by this
434	document. The amended design and plan are signed/pushed first; one material
435	Grok 4.6/high, direct Kimi K3 with
436	`KIMI_LOOP_MAX_STEPS_PER_TURN=100`, and Opus xhigh confirmation reviews the
437	complete f5b0p/f5b0 design. Only an empty P0/P1 union authorizes RED. P2 is
438	owned/dispositioned without recursive prose review. No Fable or collaboration
439	subagent may be invoked without new express user authorization.

# D.110c-0c1f5b0p bounded removed-author identity-history design

## Decision

Select a deterministic creator-authenticated Merkle AVL dictionary of currently
retired public keys and bind its root/count into every settlement checkpoint.
Select a new genesis-bound `creator-trusted-settlement-v1` profile so settlement
and retired-key continuity start at epoch zero. Do not migrate an existing
`creator-trusted-v1` room in this slice.

This remains a high-risk audited recommendation, not production authorization.
It adds no cryptographic dependency or setup and preserves the fixed creator
signer, Ed25519/SHA-256, cut/QC, ACL, anchor, snapshot, history and availability
authority. It does add a profile identifier, settlement/checkpoint schemas and
a storage-neutral retired-author registry contract. Those changes require the
combined f5b0p/f5b0 confirmation before tests-only RED.

## Authenticated dictionary

### Canonical node and root

The empty root is
`hex(hashDomain("ts-drp/retired-author-registry-empty/v1", encodeCanonical(null)))`.
Every nonempty node is the exact canonical record:

```ts
{
	author: string,
	admittedThrough: number | null,
	height: number,
	kind: "drp-retired-author-registry-node",
	left: {
		byteLength: number,
		digest: string,
		height: number,
		maxAuthor: string,
		minAuthor: string,
		subtreeSize: number,
	} | null,
	right: {
		byteLength: number,
		digest: string,
		height: number,
		maxAuthor: string,
		minAuthor: string,
		subtreeSize: number,
	} | null,
	settledThrough: number | null,
	subtreeSize: number,
	version: 1,
}
```

`author` is exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Non-null boundaries
are safe nonnegative integers; `settledThrough` may not exceed
`admittedThrough`, and `admittedThrough === null` requires
`settledThrough === null`. Height and subtree size are safe positive integers
recomputed from children. A child reference has the six exact keys shown,
positive safe byte length/height/subtree size, lowercase 64-hex digest and
canonical min/max 64-hex keys. Parent height, size and extrema must recompute
exactly from those child facts, with `left.maxAuthor < author <
right.minAuthor`. Node digest is
`hex(hashDomain("ts-drp/retired-author-registry-node/v1", exactCanonicalNodeBytes))`.
Nodes have a 1,024-byte ceiling.

The exact maximum-shaped two-child node encoded with the workspace canonical
implementation is 792 bytes, leaving 232 bytes under that ceiling.

The tree is a strict binary-search tree under UTF-16 code-unit order and an AVL
tree with balance factor -1, 0 or 1. Heights, subtree sizes, extrema, child byte
lengths, digests, key ordering and canonical bytes are recomputed along every
opened path; authenticated unopened-child metadata supplies the sibling facts
needed for parent recomputation. Empty and nonempty roots are unambiguous.

A lookup proof contains the exact root-to-terminal node bytes. The verifier
rehashes every node, follows only the branch selected by the queried key,
checks all AVL/order/metadata constraints exposed by the path, and ends either
at the unique matching key or at a null child. A truncated path, extra node,
wrong branch, foreign root, noncanonical node, digest/length mismatch,
duplicate key or malformed boundary fails closed. Membership returns the exact
prior boundaries; nonmembership returns no boundaries.

A batch witness is a canonical digest-keyed set of node bytes plus an ordered
mutation-to-path schedule. Each mutation path is verified against the root
produced by the preceding mutation, not only the original root. Deleting a node
with two children additionally opens the deterministic in-order-successor path;
missing or surplus scheduled nodes fail. Shared nodes appear once in the node
set and may be referenced repeatedly by digest.

The detached canonical witness has this exact tests-and-store boundary (it is
not a vertex, checkpoint field or public network record):

```ts
type RetiredAuthorBatchWitness = {
	kind: "drp-retired-author-registry-batch-witness";
	mutationsDigest: string;
	nodes: readonly [digest: string, exactCanonicalNodeBytes: Uint8Array][];
	priorRoot: string;
	priorRootSize: number;
	steps: readonly {
		author: string;
		lookupPath: readonly string[];
		successorPath: readonly string[];
	}[];
	version: 1;
```

both ACLs capped at 64:

```ts
	| {
			author: string;
			expected: "absent";
			kind: "assert-absent";
	  }
	| {
			author: string;
			expected: "absent";
			kind: "insert";
			admittedThrough: number | null;
			settledThrough: number | null;
	  }
	| { author: string; expected: { admittedThrough: number | null; settledThrough: number | null }; kind: "delete" };
```

occupied key and no delete accepts absent or different boundaries. An
`assert-absent` step leaves the root/count unchanged. The pure transition

deterministic single/double rotations.
Given the prior root/count, exact verified path nodes and mutations, every
conforming implementation must derive the same successor root/count and the

transmitted once.

epoch byte/capacity limits remain unchanged because proofs are creator/store
inputs, not vertices, checkpoint fields or application operations.

not need dictionary paths to authenticate the current ACL/frontiers. This does
not make a self-signed root trusted: the root/count are inside the exact creator
checkpoint, which is bound to the pinned genesis carrier, object, profile,
anchors, ACLs, close cut/QC, snapshot and history.

## Store contract and custody

Add a storage-neutral `RetiredAuthorRegistryStore` capability with opaque,
closed inputs/results for:

1. `prove({objectId,root,rootSize,authors})`: return detached canonical path
   nodes for sorted unique authors without mutating state;
2. `transactTransition({objectId,expectedRoot,expectedRootSize,retainRoots,mutations})`:
   strict-durability CAS from one registered current root, validate/rederive the
   pure transition, write all new content-addressed nodes, register the new
   root/count, and return an immutable receipt containing prior/successor
   root/count, mutation digest and exact batch-witness digest; and
3. `reclaim({objectId,currentRoot,rollbackRoots})`: mark from exactly the
   authenticated current root plus at most two authenticated rollback roots and
   delete other nodes/root registrations atomically.

The in-memory reference implementation and the browser IndexedDB implementation
are conformant. The browser owner uses a dedicated derived database/schema with
strict transactions, content-addressed `nodes` and object-scoped `roots`; it is
not an untracked side table inside AHE. Opening validates schema/incarnation.
Every read rechecks canonical bytes/digest/length. Root registrations are
exactly `candidate | current | rollback`; one serialized object may have at
most one candidate, one current and two rollback roots. Conflicting bytes for
one digest, root/count disagreement, an unclassified registered root, partial
writes, CAS mismatch or ambiguous commit poison/fail closed until authenticated
recovery determines whether the exact transition committed.

Write-before-sign ordering is mandatory:

1. authenticate current settlement checkpoint and both ACLs;
2. derive mutations and verify prior paths;
3. strictly commit/register successor root;
4. stage/sign/publish close and successor checkpoint;
5. adopt and install the authenticated successor;
6. retain current plus two rollback registry roots while matching rollback
   generations remain required; and
7. reclaim unreachable old nodes only after adoption, room-head/freshness,
   snapshot, rollback and availability gates pass.

A crash after step 3 but before signature leaves the sole inert candidate root;
retry with the same expected root/mutations/witness digest is idempotent and
may reuse it. A different transition is refused until the candidate is
authenticated and either matched to a checkpoint or discarded from the still-
current prior root. A crash
after signature but before adoption retains both roots. A missing current-root
node after restart is corruption/availability failure, never nonmembership.
Unknown write outcome is resolved by authenticating the registered exact
successor root/count/mutation/witness digest; blind retry is forbidden.

Reachable nodes under the current root grow O(R). They are explicitly counted
as an archive-tier control index. They are not loaded for ordinary issue,
publish, projection, current-checkpoint verification, restart or cold reopen.
They are required only for creator-authorized ACL membership change and may be
fetched from untrusted content storage because every byte is verified against
the creator-authenticated root. If unavailable, that ACL-changing close stalls;
ordinary room use under the current ACL continues. Phase 7 may mirror/page the
same content-addressed nodes but may not redefine their authentication.

## Genesis-bound profile and compatibility

Add profile ID `creator-trusted-settlement-v1`. Its canonical profile keys,
crypto suite, one signer, quorum and signer-set binding are identical to
`creator-trusted-v1`; only the profile ID differs. The genesis anchor's existing
`profileDigest` authenticates the choice. Internal trust values and the room's
successor authority widen to the exact union
`"creator-trusted-v1" | "creator-trusted-settlement-v1"`; the UI trust text
remains creator-trusted/not-BFT because authority did not change.

Under `creator-trusted-settlement-v1`:

- the implicit authenticated genesis sentinel supplies current ACL members
  with null boundaries and the empty retired root/size zero; there is no
  separate genesis settlement record;
- the first close emits the first settlement checkpoint directly;
- every later close requires exactly one settlement checkpoint;
- the v1 admitted-frontier aggregate and legacy creator retirement record are
  never emitted or accepted; and
- `$drp.author-settlement.v1` is mandatory from the first epoch in which a
  source disposition is needed.

Under `creator-trusted-v1`, all existing bytes and behavior remain unchanged;
settlement checkpoint/control kinds are rejected. There is no runtime option,
negotiation, downgrade or late opt-in. Existing v1 rooms cannot migrate here
because their removed-author history is not authenticated by a keyed index.
A future migration would need a separately reviewed full-history/archive proof
that reconstructs the registry without omission; Phase 7 may own that work.

The invite envelope, signer set, public key, anchor schema, CutValue, QC and
vertex envelope are unchanged. The new profile identifier is nevertheless a
public compatibility addition: old binaries reject it, and room creators must
choose it when producing the genesis profile bytes. This checkpoint does not
silently make it the default for existing callers.

This is a prospective profile-inventory amendment. Earlier Phase-3 acceptance
that supported exactly the then-existing three profiles remains immutable
historical evidence; after this slice GREEN, the supported inventory adds this
fourth creator-only sibling for newly created settlement rooms. It does not
reinterpret a prior profile, reopen its tests or claim old binaries support the
new ID.

## Settlement checkpoint amendment

Replace the previously proposed checkpoint's migration fields with this exact
shape (signature appended after signing):

```ts
{
	closedAnchorDigest,
	closedEpoch,
	commitQcRef: { byteLength, digest },
	currentAclDigest,
	cutValueDigest,
	frontiers: readonly [author, admittedThrough, settledThrough][],
	genesisAnchorDigest,
	historyRoot,
	historySize,
	kind: "drp-creator-author-settlement-state",
	objectId,
	priorCheckpointDigest,
	priorCheckpointKind: "genesis" | "settled-v1",
	protocolMajor: 3,
	retiredAuthorRegistryRoot,
	retiredAuthorRegistrySize,
	snapshotManifestDigest,
	successorAclDigest,
	successorAnchorDigest,
	successorEpoch,
	version: 1,
}
```

`retiredAuthorRegistryRoot` is the exact empty or node digest;
`retiredAuthorRegistrySize` is a safe nonnegative integer. The current active
frontier has exactly the successor ACL's sorted unique members, at most 64.
The profile must be `creator-trusted-settlement-v1`. Genesis is the sole
sentinel predecessor; every non-genesis predecessor is one adjacent settlement
checkpoint under the same profile/object/genesis. There is no
`admitted-v1` predecessor, v1 migration branch or legacy-retirement bridge.
The maximum-shaped signed checkpoint with 64 full frontier entries, a 256-code-
unit object ID, maximum safe integers, full digests and a 64-byte creator
signature encodes to 7,064 bytes with the workspace canonical implementation,
leaving 1,128 bytes under the unchanged 8,192-byte ceiling. Codec RED must pin
that exact measurement and adjacent over-limit/count rejection; the ceiling is
not raised.

## Failure and adversarial matrix

| Case                                                         | Required result                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| globally fresh key                                           | verified nonmembership; null boundaries; first sequence zero                                |
| removed key re-added                                         | membership restores exact boundaries; next sequence strictly greater than admitted boundary |
| key retained across ACL roles                                | active boundary copied; no dictionary mutation                                              |
| remove then re-add within one staged ACL                     | retained by current/final membership; no reset                                              |
| active key also found in retired root                        | checkpoint/transition invalid                                                               |
| insertion finds occupied key                                 | fail closed; no checkpoint signature                                                        |
| deletion finds absent/different boundaries                   | fail closed; no checkpoint signature                                                        |
| stale, substituted, truncated, reordered or foreign proof    | fail closed before store mutation/signature                                                 |
| noncanonical node or wrong digest/length/height/size/balance | fail closed and classify store corruption                                                   |
| store unavailable                                            | membership-changing close unavailable; no fallback-to-fresh                                 |
| crash before registry commit                                 | old root remains current; retry from durable truth                                          |
| crash after registry commit before checkpoint signature      | inert candidate root; idempotent exact retry or later GC                                    |
| crash after signature before adoption                        | both roots retained; old checkpoint authoritative                                           |
| adoption succeeds before reclamation                         | new root authoritative; rollback roots still retained                                       |
| premature/misbound reclamation                               | CAS/reachability refusal; no live-node deletion                                             |
| old profile receives new carrier                             | unsupported/mixed-profile rejection                                                         |
| new profile omits settlement/registry carrier                | fail closed                                                                                 |
| legacy room attempts late opt-in                             | explicit unsupported migration failure                                                      |
| untrusted current checkpoint nominates its own key/root      | rejected by pinned-genesis creator-trust opener                                             |
| valid but stale checkpoint/root                              | rejected by the existing external room-head freshness floor                                 |

## Bounds and golden-path accounting

- Active settlement checkpoint: O(64) frontier entries plus one root/count;
  independent of epoch, rebase count and retired-author count.
- Ordinary hot issue/publish and cold reopen: no dictionary traversal; fixed
  checkpoint plus existing current/two-rollback closure law.
- Membership-changing close: O(M log R) verified reads/writes for `M <= 128`;
  no O(epoch) or O(history) replay.
- Reachable registry backing: O(R) entries/bytes for currently retired distinct
  keys, plus copy-on-write nodes reachable from at most two rollback roots and
  at most one serialized candidate root.
  This is separately reported in the durable census by entry count, node count
  and bytes. It is never counted as application archive or hidden bootstrap.
- Re-adding a retired key deletes its live registry entry; removing it later
  inserts the newer boundary. Repeated churn of a fixed author set therefore
  keeps current-root logical entries bounded by that set, while obsolete path
  nodes are reclaimable after rollback gates.
- The ≥100 same-room transition test includes remove/re-add, fresh additions,
  restarts before/after registry commit and adoption, selected prune boundaries,
  exact root/count recomputation, current/rollback reachability census and a
  fresh-process post-GC memory gate. It does not claim O(1) archival registry
  bytes under unbounded distinct-key churn.

## TDD slices and gates

After the combined design confirmation is empty at P0/P1:

1. **f5b0p-a protocol dictionary/profile RED→GREEN.** Tests-only RED exercises
   empty/member/nonmember proofs, deterministic AVL rotations, batch updates,
   stale/substituted proofs, root/count/metadata corruption, maximum 128-key
   transition, profile acceptance/rejection and the measured 64-frontier
   checkpoint ceiling. GREEN is confined to pure codecs/verifiers/profile
   unions/exports and adds no storage or room behavior.
2. **f5b0p-b store RED→GREEN.** Tests-only RED freezes in-memory and browser
   conformance, strict write-before-sign receipt semantics, idempotence,
   ambiguous commit recovery, corruption poison, current/two-rollback
   reachability GC and unavailable-node refusal. GREEN adds the neutral store,
   memory implementation, dedicated IndexedDB implementation/schema and
   internal room construction plumbing; it does not integrate creator close.
3. **f5b0a-d and f5b.** Resume the already frozen settlement carrier, Node,
   room and pruning slices, amended so new-profile genesis has no v1 migration
   or legacy retirement. Creator integration uses the genuine ACL diff and
   registry store before signing. Each retains its causal RED and focused,
   static, retained and isolated GREEN gates.

The combined functional RED must fail through the real product path: create a
`creator-trusted-settlement-v1` room, remove an author after admitted/settled
activity, close/adopt/restart, re-add the same key and attempt sequence zero.
It must also show a truly fresh key starts at zero. Fixture-injected registry
roots or tests-only appearance facts cannot satisfy causality.

GREEN/retained acceptance includes exact same-key continuation, fresh-key zero,
mixed ACL role retention, 64-member/128-mutation bounds, store-death crash
matrix, two rollback roots, unavailable registry refusal, ordinary reopen with
the registry store absent, no v1 behavior change, old-binary profile rejection,
current checkpoint byte ceiling, ≥100 real same-room epochs, bounded active
checkpoint/owner census, explicit O(R) registry census, and Phase-7 cold join
using current authenticated checkpoint plus archived application history.

No production edit, RED, long campaign or multi-epoch run is authorized by this
document. The amended design and plan are signed/pushed first; one material
Grok 4.6/high, direct Kimi K3 with
`KIMI_LOOP_MAX_STEPS_PER_TURN=100`, and Opus xhigh confirmation reviews the
complete f5b0p/f5b0 design. Only an empty P0/P1 union authorizes RED. P2 is
owned/dispositioned without recursive prose review. No Fable or collaboration
subagent may be invoked without new express user authorization.

308		frontiers: readonly [
309			author: string,
310			admittedThrough: number | null,
311			settledThrough: number | null,
312		][],
313		genesisAnchorDigest,
314		historyRoot,
315		historySize,
316		kind: "drp-creator-author-settlement-state",
317		objectId,
318		priorCheckpointDigest,
319		priorCheckpointKind: "genesis" | "settled-v1",
320		protocolMajor: 3,
321		retiredAuthorRegistryRoot,
322		retiredAuthorRegistrySize,
323		snapshotManifestDigest,
324		successorAclDigest,
325		successorAnchorDigest,
326		successorEpoch,
327		version: 1,
328	}
329	```
330	
331	The record adds `detachedCreatorSignature` after signing. The existing opaque
332	creator signing request pattern is reused; callers never receive an arbitrary
333	digest-signing primitive. Frontiers are strictly code-unit sorted, unique, and
334	contain at most the 64 members of the successor ACL (not only writers).
335	`admittedThrough` and `settledThrough` are distinct capabilities. A member
336	that loses write permission but retains another ACL role therefore keeps both
337	boundaries.
338	
339	`retiredAuthorRegistryRoot` and `retiredAuthorRegistrySize` bind the exact
340	Merkle AVL state frozen in the f5b0p design. A fully removed key is inserted
341	with its final admitted/settled boundaries; a re-added key is deleted and its
342	boundaries return to the active vector. Verified nonmembership is the only way
343	a new key begins with null boundaries. Ordinary openers authenticate the
344	creator-signed root/count without loading dictionary nodes; the creator
345	verifies O(log R) paths only for membership-changing ACL transitions.
346	
347	The record binds the current and successor creator trust, object/genesis,
348	adjacent epochs/anchors, both ACLs, cut digest, commit QC, snapshot manifest,
349	and the history root/size produced for the current graph. The cut independently
350	contains the same snapshot and history facts. Any mismatch fails closed. Under
351	`creator-trusted-settlement-v1`, the predecessor is exactly one genesis
352	sentinel or one prior settlement checkpoint; mixed, duplicate, skipped, stale
353	or downgraded predecessors fail. A `creator-trusted-v1` room never accepts this
354	checkpoint.
355	
356	For each successor ACL member, the creator begins with the prior authenticated
357	settled boundary (or null), groups the complete current close graph by exact
358	`(author, authorSequence, digest)`, and authenticates settlement statements.
359	A settled slot is accounted only by exactly one graph vertex identity or
360	exactly one same-author source disposition. A graph/source digest mismatch,
361	same-slot equivocation, duplicate source, invalid causal replacement,
362	cross-scope ref, or malformed statement stops settlement advancement for that
363	author at the last exact adjacent slot. It does not abort the close or change
364	another author's result. Creator-owned duplicate/regression errors keep their
365	current fail-closed behavior.
366	
367	The admitted boundary separately advances only across exact adjacent graph
368	slots and never across a disposition. At settlement-profile genesis every
369	active member begins with both boundaries null. In later checkpoints both are
370	monotone and neither can regress. The creator's own author participates in the
371	same settlement scan. Settlement-profile closures contain neither the v1
372	aggregate nor the legacy creator-retirement record; the settlement checkpoint
373	is the sole per-author recovery authority from the first close. Existing v1
374	rooms retain their exact existing aggregate/retirement behavior and cannot
375	late-opt-in in this slice.
376	
377	The scan advances from `prior + 1` (or zero) through exact adjacent accounted
378	slots; a control vertex's own author sequence is an ordinary graph slot. It
379	never takes an observed maximum and never advances across unknown evidence.
380	The creator signs the resulting vector and close proceeds even when one
381	foreign boundary cannot advance, preserving f5a's per-author liveness.
382	
383	## Recovery semantics and pruning
384	
385	The admitted and settled frontiers are different
386	capabilities and have different consumers:
387	
388	- `creator-trusted-v1` retains its existing `covered-historical` behavior
389	  byte-for-byte;
390	- `creator-trusted-settlement-v1` begins at genesis with null admitted/settled
391	  boundaries and never imports a v1 admitted frontier;
392	- under a verified settlement checkpoint, any same-author issuance row at or
393	  below `settledThrough` is **terminal**. It is never republished, rebased,
394	  reduced or used as application evidence, regardless of its digest; and
395	- a valid row above `settledThrough` and at or below `admittedThrough` retains
396	  the existing covered-historical behavior; any other row above the settled
397	  boundary retains displaced/rebase behavior. Both require a later signed
398	  settlement statement before becoming terminal.
399	
400	The terminal rule is why an unseen or substituted row below the new prefix
401	cannot gain authority. The checkpoint authenticates a decision boundary, not
402	membership of arbitrary row bytes. Same-slot equivocation remains evidence and
403	cannot advance a future boundary, but neither fork is applied after settlement.
404	
405	Control and source issuance rows remain in issuance/live-journal custody until
406	a later authenticated checkpoint covers their sequence. f5b0d adds one
407	storage-neutral `pruneAuthenticatedSettledPrefix` contract, its in-memory and
408	browser implementations, and conformance vectors. Node may call it only after
409	durable checkpoint staging, verified successor adoption, rollback-generation
410	retention, availability, expected-head/revision, and exact checkpoint-author
411	boundary checks. Its transaction compare-and-deletes issued/outbox rows at or
412	below `settledThrough` across any number of old epochs and advances the
413	existing pruned watermark monotonically. Unlike legacy
414	`prunePublishedPrefix`, it does not require every selected row to share one
415	`closedEpoch` or to be published: the authenticated settled capability is the
416	authority that pending and substituted rows are terminal. It does require the
417	expected lineage-next and prior-pruned watermark to match, and ambiguity or
418	partial deletion fails closed. The legacy single-epoch method and all v1 paths
419	remain unchanged.
420	
421	Receipt bytes remain in archived RFC 9162 history for audit but are not needed
422	for ordinary cold reopen. Active control state is one current checkpoint with
423	at most 64 frontier triples, the existing fixed rollback
424	generations and compact history peaks, plus current-epoch control vertices
425	already bounded by `maxEpochVertices`, `maxEpochBytes`, `maxPendingEntries`
426	and `maxPendingBytes`. No state grows with epoch count or number of completed
427	rebases. Manual-review rows remain explicit application/outbox debt and stop
428	only that author's boundary; they are not copied into another hidden store.
429	The active checkpoint stays O(64), while reachable retired-author dictionary
430	nodes are an explicit O(R) archive-tier control index, counted separately and
431	unnecessary for ordinary cold reopen. They are needed only by the creator when
432	membership changes; unavailability stalls that close rather than weakening
433	freshness.
434	
435	## Compatibility and genesis-profile boundary
436	
437	The application adds
438	`hasDisplacedOperation(projection, operation): boolean`; it is required only
439	for a settlement-profile room. The function is called twice over the same
440	detached authenticated inputs and disagreement fails closed. It does not sign,
441	admit or settle anything.
442	
443	The creator selects exact profile ID `creator-trusted-settlement-v1` in the
444	canonical profile bytes before genesis. Its signer set, quorum, crypto suite
445	and creator-trusted/not-BFT UI meaning are identical to
446	`creator-trusted-v1`; the genesis anchor's existing `profileDigest` binds the
447	choice. Settlement state starts at genesis with the active ACL's null
448	frontiers and the empty retired-author root/count. Every close uses the new
449	checkpoint and control rules. Old binaries reject the unsupported profile.
450	
451	An existing `creator-trusted-v1` room emits and consumes only the existing
452	admitted frontier/creator retirement and cannot late-opt-in. There is no
453	runtime option, negotiation, fallback or automatic migration. A future
454	migration requires separately reviewed authenticated full-history author-index
455	construction. Existing bytes are never relabelled.
456	
457	This is a protocol/closure-schema/profile and public compatibility change but
458	not a protobuf/wire-envelope or authority change. It adds no dependency and
459	uses the current Ed25519, canonical and RFC 9162 implementations.
460	
461	## Crash, attack and failure matrix
462	
463	The implementation and retained tests must prove:
464	
465	| Boundary or attack                                                                  | Required result                                                                                                |
466	| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
467	| crash before replacement issue                                                      | source stays pending; restart selects it once                                                                  |
468	| crash after some replacements                                                       | exact accepted identities are reused/deduped; missing replacements issue once                                  |
469	| crash before control transaction                                                    | no source completion; restart authors one statement                                                            |
470	| unknown control transaction outcome                                                 | application issue halts; reopen enumerates durable truth before retry                                          |
471	| control journaled but unpublished                                                   | restart republishes it; source remains pending until publication succeeds                                      |
472	| control published, creator has not admitted it                                      | local source may be complete, but no checkpoint advances; retained replay remains                              |
473	| close stages before source-local completion                                         | admitted statement may advance; restart terminalizes source from checkpoint and completes/prunes only at gates |
474	| close/adoption fails                                                                | old checkpoint remains authoritative; no prune                                                                 |
475	| adoption succeeds before prune                                                      | new terminal boundary is authoritative; rollback generations and availability still gate prune                 |
476	| malformed/cross-object/cross-author/cross-epoch/stale/future ref                    | statement rejected before append                                                                               |
477	| replacement missing, reordered, substituted, not same-author or not causal ancestor | source not settled                                                                                             |
478	| replacement batch count/index/digest mismatch                                       | source not settled                                                                                             |
479	| duplicate/conflicting receipt                                                       | affected author does not advance; creator-local conflict keeps exact hard failure                              |
480	| zero-intent join/causalJoin/ACL gap                                                 | exact signed source disposition advances only that slot; no application effect inferred                        |
481	| settlement vertex in close graph                                                    | included in charges/frontier/close-set/history, excluded exactly from application fold                         |
482	| row substitution at or below settled prefix                                         | row is terminal and never applied                                                                              |
483	| row above prefix                                                                    | ordinary authenticated displacement handling; never silently terminal                                          |
484	| legacy v1 room receives settlement carrier/profile                                  | exact unsupported/mixed-profile rejection; existing behavior unchanged                                         |
485	| creator's own displaced row in settlement profile                                   | settles through the same control/checkpoint path; no legacy retirement owner exists                            |
486	| same-key removal/re-entry                                                           | registry membership restores the exact boundary; reset is rejected                                             |
487	| genuinely fresh key                                                                 | registry nonmembership permits null boundary and sequence zero                                                 |
488	| registry proof/store unavailable                                                    | membership-changing close stalls; no fallback-to-fresh                                                         |
489	| cross-object migration import                                                       | remains explicit manual-review debt; no fabricated same-object replacement                                     |
490	| manual review                                                                       | no receipt, no false settlement, other authors may close                                                       |
491	| incompatible/mixed/downgraded closure                                               | successor open/advance rejects                                                                                 |
492	
493	## Resolved identity-history design prerequisite
494	
495	The first review proved that the carrier and checkpoint cannot safely infer
496	that an ACL key absent from the immediately prior frontier is globally new.
497	The f5b0p audit confirms no dormant current owner can do so and selects the
498	Merkle AVL retired-author dictionary and genesis-bound settlement profile in
499	`.logs/d110c-0c1f5b0p-design-e6a67013/design.md`.
500	
501	The active checkpoint holds only one authenticated root/count plus the current
502	64-member vector. Ordinary reopen does not read the dictionary. Membership-
503	changing creator close verifies O(log R) paths from untrusted storage; reachable
504	backing is an explicit O(R) archive-tier control index, not hidden active or
505	bootstrap state. That information-theoretic growth is accepted only if the
506	governing confirmation agrees it satisfies the durable-census contract. If
507	review instead requires O(1) durable bytes under unbounded distinct-key churn,
508	stop at design and open a cryptographic accumulator/recursive-proof prerequisite;
509	do not implement a disguised tombstone list.
510	
511	## TDD implementation slices
512	
513	After the combined design confirmation has an empty P0/P1 union,
514	implementation is split at natural owners without repeated plan ceremony:
515	
516	1. **f5b0p-a — protocol dictionary/profile.** RED freezes the exact Merkle AVL
517	   node/proof/update grammar, deterministic rotations, profile union,
518	   genesis-empty state, root/count checkpoint fields and the measured
519	   64-frontier byte ceiling. GREEN is pure codecs/verifiers/profile plumbing;
520	   no store or creator-close behavior.
521	2. **f5b0p-b — retired-author registry store.** RED freezes the neutral
522	   contract plus memory/browser strict durability, idempotence, ambiguous
523	   outcome recovery, corruption refusal and current/two-rollback reachability
524	   GC. GREEN adds the dedicated store/schema; it does not hide nodes in AHE.
525	3. **f5b0a — protocol carrier and checkpoint codecs.** RED freezes exact
526	   canonical shapes, byte/count limits, signature/domain behavior,
527	   genesis/settled predecessor rules, global reservation, old/mixed-profile
528	   rejection and opaque signing custody. GREEN is confined to protocol-v3
529	   registry/codecs/exports, issuer-side discrimination, and conformance.
530	4. **f5b0b — Node admission, close-graph split and durable settlement
531	   transaction.** RED uses real
532	   signed vertices and durable issuance/live-journal stores for normal,
533	   restart, outcome-unknown, partial publication, duplicate and malformed
534	   cases, plus control∪application close-map equality and reducer exclusion.
535	   GREEN adds the settlement-specific authentication/recovery paths,
536	   `settleRebaseSources()`, and exact Node-owned close split; compaction is a
537	   retained invariant/test owner, not a widened reducer. No room policy or
538	   creator-frontier logic.
539	5. **f5b0c — room disposition orchestration.** RED drives the real rebase
540	   outbox through expire, manual-review, already-present, rebase, transform,
541	   indexed batching, zero-intent control sources, migration-import refusal and
542	   crash boundaries. GREEN adds only the deterministic
543	   projection-presence query and internal result plumbing; public `issue()` is
544	   unchanged.
545	6. **f5b0d — authenticated settled-prefix reclamation.** RED freezes the new
546	   storage-neutral CAS/delete contract and conformance across mixed epochs,
547	   pending/published/substituted rows, stale lineage/watermark, partial failure,
548	   rollback and v1 noninterference. GREEN owns issuance-store, memory model,
549	   browser implementation, closed-epoch cleanup integration and bounded
550	   retained census.
551	7. **f5b — creator settlement and recovery integration.** The already-owned
552	   causal RED covers rebase and honest delivery gaps, genesis gap, same-slot
553	   regression, membership re-entry, at least two later close/adopt cycles,
554	   creator and non-creator rows, restart and cold reopen. GREEN applies dual
555	   per-author advancement only under the genesis-bound settlement profile,
556	   emits no v1 aggregate/legacy retirement there, and owns terminal recovery
557	   and gated pruning. It derives the real current/successor ACL diff, commits the exact
558	   registry transition before checkpoint signing and keeps current plus two
559	   rollback roots.
560	
561	Each sub-slice uses one causal tests-only RED before its production GREEN,
562	focused/static/retained/isolated gates with complete logs, signed commits and
563	pushed refs. The final f5b review inspects the complete signed design→RED→GREEN
564	history with Grok 4.6/high, direct Kimi K3 at 100 steps and Opus xhigh. Because
565	the design review is the unique high-risk authority/API checkpoint, the three
566	implementation sub-slices do not recursively reopen the architecture unless a
567	RED contradicts this matrix or production work requires a different wire,
568	authority, dependency, threshold or API.
569	
570	## Acceptance and stop rules
571	
572	No production edit or RED runs before the amended design confirmation has an
573	empty P0/P1 union. P2 receives an owner/disposition without prose-only
574	recursion. If review shows that a normal signed control vertex cannot preserve
575	the current causality/capacity contract, that author abandonment is
576	insufficient authority, that the genesis-profile boundary is unsafe, or that
577	the explicit O(R) archive-tier registry violates the accepted durable-census
578	contract, stop and reslice the exact prerequisite rather than implementing a
579	nearby substitute.
580	
581	The complete GREEN must demonstrate genuine source rows and signed control
582	vertices through ordinary publication, close/adopt, restart and cold reopen;
583	exact state, ACL, authority, anchor, history, archive and operation accounting;
584	no same-anchor double close; unchanged `creator-trusted-v1` behavior;
585	fail-closed old/mixed peers; authenticated same-key continuation and fresh-key
586	zero; retained f2/f4/f5a and D.108-D.110 lifecycle behavior; bounded active
587	checkpoint/runtime census plus explicit O(R) registry accounting; and
588	fresh-process repeated same-room memory in the later ≥100-transition gate.
589	Tests-only receipt/registry injection or synthetic checkpoint bytes cannot
590	satisfy the end-to-end RED/GREEN.
